rv.q: The show's strength is the potent and courageous ensemble acting, as adroitly and generously directed by Kazemi (it will get yet better too).
Raven’s “A Lie of the Mind” is a similarly spectacular entry to Chicago’s storied theater history.
Shepard's play, brilliantly mounted by Raven Theatre under the direction of Azar Kazemi, does indeed overwhelm its audiences with cruelty at times...
The effect is a fully realized production that feels fresh and relevant.
At Raven Theatre, director Azar Kazemi creates a powerhouse production of a play that deserves more attention as a Shepard masterwork.
Lie of the Mind is not a play for an entertaining night out: it is an excavation of two broken families that will reverberate.
But A LIE OF THE MIND, which runs short of three hours, now feels simply like a lengthy journey to Crazy Town.

Raven Theatre's production, sharply directed by Azar Kazemi, on an interesting set designed by Lauren M. Nichols, allows us to see several different locations, and yet switch from one to another with no lost time.

cn.t: Raven Theatre's muscular, blistering production of Shepard's challenging family saga earns praise for its intensity and performances, though some find the 1985 play less resonant than the playwright's tighter works.
